title: Count No-Zero Pairs That Sum to N
summary: Count pairs of no-zero integers (a, b) such that their sum equals n, where a and b are positive integers without the digit 0.
statement: Count pairs of no-zero integers (a, b) such that their sum equals n, where a and b are positive integers without the digit 0.
constraints: Both a and b are positive and their decimal representations contain no zero digit.
hints: Process the decimal addition from least significant digit to most significant digit.
Track the carry and whether each addend still has digits; active digits are one through nine, while a number may end after its first digit.
A digit DP tries compatible digit pairs at each position and requires both numbers and the final carry to end together.
The state records exactly the information passed to the next column, so every no-zero ordered addition is counted once.
editorial: The state records exactly the information passed to the next column, so every no-zero ordered addition is counted once.

tests.explanation: Eight ordered pairs from (2,9) through (9,2) qualify; pairs containing ten do not.
